The '''Derby d'Italia''' ({{langx|en|Derby of Italy}}) is the name of the [[association football|football]] [[List of sports rivalries|derby]] between [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] of [[Milan]] and [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] of [[Turin]]. The term was coined in 1967 by Italian sports journalist [[Gianni Brera]].<ref name="guardian"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Derby d'Italia: Historical look-back|url=http://www.footballitaliano.co.uk/p6_66_34_derby-ditalia-historical-look-back.html|publisher=footballitaliano.co.uk|date=20 November 2008|access-date=7 September 2012|archive-date=5 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180805052159/http://www.footballitaliano.co.uk/p6_66_34_derby-ditalia-historical-look-back.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The teams are from the two biggest cities in [[Northern Italy]]. Both teams have fans across Italy, and there are numerous fan clubs of Juventus in [[Piedmont]] and Inter in [[Lombardy]] (including in the two cities).<ref>{{cite news|title=OFFICIAL FAN CLUB|url=https://www.juventus.com/it/fans/official-fan-club/trova-juventus-official-fan-club.php |publisher=Juventus FC|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Trova un Inter Club |url=https://www.inter.it/it/inter_club/cerca-inter-club |website=inter.it|publisher=Inter Milan|language=it}}</ref>

Both clubs are among the [[List of football clubs by competitive honours won|most successful football clubs in the world]].

==History==
The matchup between Juventus and Inter is perhaps the most intense match in Italy between two teams from different cities, historically since the 1950s and 60s, and especially after the ''[[2006 Italian football scandal|Calciopoli]]'' which saw Juventus stripped of their league title from [[2005–06 Serie A|2005–06]] and given to Inter.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/2007/08/sezioni/sport/calcio/tifo-contro/tifo-contro/tifo-contro.html|title=Calcio, va di moda tifare contro|publisher=repubblica.it|author=Luigi Ceccarini|date=24 August 2007|access-date=4 February 2017|language=it}}</ref>

After a field invasion due to the overflowing stands<ref name=":0">{{cite news|url=https://storiedicalcio.altervista.org/blog/juventus_inter_9-1_boniperti.html|title=Juventus-Inter 9-1, gloria effimera|author=storiedicalcio.altervista.org|language=it}}</ref> during a derby fixture in the [[1960–61 Serie A|1960–61 season]], [[Lega Calcio]] awarded the match to Inter but later [[FIGC]] overturned the decision and ordered a replay, much to the fury of Inter president [[Angelo Moratti]] and club supporters. Moratti accused the Italian football association of favouritism due to the [[Agnelli family|Agnelli]] family's influence, as [[Umberto Agnelli]] was FIGC president at that time. In protest, Inter fielded their youth players for the replay and were thrashed 9–1. Juventus striker [[Omar Sívori]] scored six goals in the match and went on to win the [[Ballon d'Or]] that year,<ref name="guardian">{{cite news|title=Juventus make their point in engrossing Derby D'Italia|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/nov/05/europeanfootball.internazionale|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=5 November 2007}}</ref> Inter only goal was scored by a young [[Sandro Mazzola]].
[[File:Morini Boninsegna 1973-74.jpg|thumb|left|270px|[[Roberto Boninsegna]] tackled by [[Francesco Morini]] during a ''derby d'Italia'' in 1974.]]

During the [[1997–98 Serie A|1997–98]] fixture at the [[Stadio delle Alpi]] there was controversy over referee [[Piero Ceccarini]]'s decisions, in particular not to award a penalty for [[Mark Iuliano]]'s foul on Inter forward [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] in the direct clash between the two teams decisive for the title with Inter behind only 1 point with 4 games left. Juventus, up 1–0 at the time of the incident, were after few seconds awarded a penalty which was missed by [[Alessandro Del Piero]]; Juventus won the game 1–0 and with this secured the scudetto with five points ahead. The incident caused heated arguments in the [[Italian parliament]] during a publicly broadcast "[[question time]]" session in April 1998.<ref name="guardian"/><ref>{{cite book|title=Forza Italia: The Fall and Rise of Italian Football|page=295|date=2007|publisher=[[Ebury Publishing]]|isbn=9781448117642|last=Agnew|first=Paddy}}</ref> Domenico Gramazio of the [[National Alliance (Italy)|National Alliance]] reportedly shouted "They are all thieves!" at fellow politician and former Juventus player [[Massimo Mauro]] of the ruling [[Democrats of the Left]], prompting [[Chamber of Deputies (Italy)|Chamber of Deputies]] member and then-Deputy Prime Minister [[Walter Veltroni]] to comment, "We are not at a stadium. This is a spectacle that is unworthy, embarrassing and grotesque...". The session had to be suspended and several politicians were later penalised as a result.<ref name="BBC">{{cite news|title=Political football, Italian style|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/85688.stm|work=[[BBC News]]|date=28 April 1998}}</ref>

During the days leading up to the derby on 5 December 2009 in Turin, there were fears about the [[Juventus F.C. ultras|Juventus ultras]] abusing Inter's Italian striker [[Mario Balotelli]] (who is of Ghanaian descent) due to a history of racial abuse from fans. Juventus chairman [[Jean-Claude Blanc]] and Mirella Scirea, widow of Juventus legend [[Gaetano Scirea]], wrote to the ultra groups and publicly urged fans to refrain from using racist chants.<ref>{{cite news|title=Derby weekend lights up with fireworks on and off the field|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2009/dec/07/juventus-inter-serie-a-derby|work=[[The Guardian newspaper|The Guardian]]|date=7 December 2009}}</ref> When Inter's players arrived in Turin, the team bus was pelted with eggs by some Juventus fans. The match itself was marred by seven bookings, a red card and a number of heated on-pitch altercations, in particular between Juve goalkeeper [[Gianluigi Buffon]] and Inter midfielder [[Thiago Motta]]. Inter manager [[José Mourinho]] was dismissed in the first half for arguing with the referee.<ref>{{cite news|title=Juve slam brakes on Inter|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=929856.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604150402/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=929856.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 4, 2011|publisher=[[UEFA|uefa.com]]|date=5 December 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Report: Juventus vs Internazionale|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=278358&league=ITA.1&cc=5901|work=[[ESPN|espn.com]]|date=6 December 2009|access-date=26 February 2010|archive-date=4 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604120614/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=278358&league=ITA.1&cc=5901|url-status=dead}}</ref> A second-half winner from [[Claudio Marchisio]] re-opened the ''Scudetto'' race as Inter's lead was cut to five points.

Juventus and Inter were matched up for the semi-final of the [[2015–16 Coppa Italia]], where Juventus won the opening leg 3–0 at home in Turin on 27 January 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/juventus/2016/01/27/news/juventus_batte_inter-132188450/|title=Juventus-Inter 3-0: si risveglia Morata, i bianconeri ipotecano la finale|publisher=repubblica.it|author=Francesco Carci|date=27 January 2016|language=it}}</ref> In the return leg on 3 March 2016, Inter won 3–0 in Milan at home to tie 3–3 on aggregate and force a [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]], which Juventus ultimately won 5–3 to move on to the [[2016 Coppa Italia Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/juventus/2016/03/03/news/inter-juventus_6-5_dcr_bianconeri_in_finale_con_l_affanno-134665505/|title=Coppa Italia, Inter a un soffio dall'impresa: Juventus in finale solo ai rigori|publisher=repubblica.it|author=Jacopo Manfredi|date=3 March 2016|language=it}}</ref>

• '''Total:''' Juventus with '''54''' higher finishes, Inter with '''39''' higher finishes (as of the end of the 2025–26 season). No head-to-head in [[2006-07 Serie A|2007]], since Juventus was in [[Serie B]].

'''Notes''':
* [[1945–46 Italian Football Championship]] is not included in [[Football records and statistics in Italy|Serie A statistics]].
* Both teams finished with the same number of points in [[1989–90 Serie A|1990]], but Inter had better goal difference: Inter  finished in third place, Juventus in fourth.
* Due to the [[Calciopoli]] scandal, Juventus' [[2004–05 Serie A|2004–05 title]] was voided, while in the [[2005–06 Serie A|2005–06 season]] Juventus was relegated and the title was awarded to Inter.
